# reclaimit

> Developer-aware disk cleanup CLI and terminal UI written in Go.

reclaimit finds regenerable developer artifacts, groups them by Git repository
or path, and lets users review candidates before deletion.

## Verified capabilities

- 17 cleanup categories covering JavaScript, Python, Rust, frontend builds,
  Bun, pip, pipx, generic caches, and macOS metadata.
- Plain-text, Markdown, and JSON reports with per-candidate safety notes.
- `conservative`, `balanced`, and `expanded` risk profiles for choosing how
  broad candidate detection should be.
- Interactive terminal UI.
- Read-only analysis and non-destructive cleanup dry runs.
- Read-only `doctor` diagnostics for local installation and runtime checks.
- One configurable worker ceiling across the complete scan, with interrupt-safe
  cancellation of queued traversal work.
- Pre-delete checks for path identity, type, measured size, and modification
  snapshot, followed by an atomic same-filesystem quarantine and revalidation.
  Changed data is preserved with a reported recovery path.
- Prebuilt release archives for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- Installer verification against the release SHA-256 manifest before any
  destination write.
- Versioned JSON selection manifests with fail-closed root and candidate
  identity validation.

## Install

Install the latest release from https://github.com/svg153/reclaimit/releases/latest.
For a source install, use Go 1.25.12 or newer:

```bash
go install github.com/svg153/reclaimit/cmd/reclaimit@v0.7.0
```

Release archives include SHA-256 checksums and the installer verifies them before writing a destination file.

## Example

```bash
reclaimit analyze --root "$HOME/code" --format json --out report.json
reclaimit analyze --root "$HOME/code" --format json --anonymous
reclaimit doctor
reclaimit clean --root "$HOME/code" --include-category python-venv --dry-run
```

## Safety

Deletion is irreversible and cannot be transactional on a normal filesystem.
Symbolic links and special files are skipped. Users should review dry-run output
and keep backups for valuable data. Each cleanup candidate includes a
`safety_note` in JSON reports and a human-readable rationale in plain-text and
Markdown reports.
Use `--risk-profile conservative` to exclude review-level categories such as
generic caches and application environments.
Use `--anonymous` for shareable reports with local roots, paths, groups,
mismatches, recovery paths, cleanup previews, and TUI reproduction commands
redacted. Selection manifests still contain operational paths and must not be
shared publicly.
